input.question: Why aren’t we allowed to lower the salaries of politicians? So that we can be sure that they are running not for money but because they really want to serve?
input.ground_truth: Mostly because it would become a tool to control the have-nots. Lower the the salaries of politicians until it a burden even for those who want to serve. Net result is that the only people who would run wouldn't be the people who want to serve, but the people who are financially able. Side note. Most of the money politician make come from things other than their salary. Book deals, speeches, etc...

If you say, “I’ll only let you help if you don’t get any extra crayons,” some friends might still want to help because they like coloring with you, but others might not want to help at all, because they don’t get anything extra.

If you lower the salaries of politicians too much, some good people might not want to run for office because they need money to live. And sometimes, people who really want to help might not be able to run because they can’t live without enough money.

Also, if we lower their salaries too much, it might be hard for them to do their job well, because they need things like a home and food.

So, instead of lowering salaries, we try to make rules to make sure politicians are honest and really want to help people, not just get rich. That way, we can have leaders who care about doing a good job, not just about getting more money.
